page: Amazon Web Services m7i.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the performance of the m7i.2xlarge mostly within the average range for its hardware class. It demonstrates standard capabilities in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, alongside average memory bandwidth speeds of 50.51 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for matrix mathematics. While it shows strong performance in Geekbench text processing, it exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and text generation tasks using medium-sized 7B language models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of specialized memory or compute-optimized hardware. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are externalized to network-attached volumes. This instance is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications that require stable, dedicated CPU allocation and modern DDR5 memory performance.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of DDR5 RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It utilizes a dedicated CPU allocation with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance delivers average performance across most standard benchmarks, including stress-ng and Geekbench, with a notable strength in text processing. However, it shows lower efficiency in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-sized LLM text generation. With a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, this instance provides a balanced resource profile qualitatively optimized for general-purpose workloads, such as web serving, database operations, and software compilation, where local NVMe storage is not a strict requirement.
